record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Describe the idempotents in the semigroup of quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups. What is its cardinality?

evidence.quote: 1.14∗ . Describe the idempotents in the semigroup of quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups. What is its cardinality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An ℓ-group (lattice-ordered group) is a group $G$ equipped with a lattice order such that the group operation distributes over the lattice operations on both sides; equivalently, $a \le b$ implies $cad \le cbd$ for all $a,b,c,d \in G$. A quasi-variety of ℓ-groups is a class of ℓ-groups closed under isomorphisms, substructures, direct products, and ultraproducts (equivalently, axiomatizable by quasi-identities in the language of ℓ-groups). The collection $\mathbf{Q}$ of all quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups carries a binary product: for quasi-varieties $\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{V}$, define
$$\mathcal{U}\cdot\mathcal{V} = \mathrm{Q}\bigl(\{G : \text{there exists a convex normal ℓ-subgroup } N \trianglelefteq G \text{ with } N \in \mathcal{U} \text{ and } G/N \in \mathcal{V}\}\bigr),$$
where $\mathrm{Q}(\cdot)$ denotes the quasi-variety generated by the indicated class. This product is associative, making $(\mathbf{Q}, \cdot)$ a semigroup.

(a) Describe (give a structural characterization of) all idempotent elements of the semigroup $(\mathbf{Q}, \cdot)$, i.e., all quasi-varieties $\mathcal{U}$ of ℓ-groups satisfying $\mathcal{U} \cdot \mathcal{U} = \mathcal{U}$.

(b) Determine the cardinality of the set of such idempotents.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this problem. It is known that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups, but a structural description of the idempotents of the multiplication semigroup of quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups, together with a determination of their cardinality, does not appear to have been established in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-varieties of lattice ordered groups
status_evidence.snippet: There are 2^{aleph_0} pairwise incomparable quasi-varieties of lattice-ordered groups containing the maximal variety; the lattice of l-group varieties is a sublattice of the lattice of quasi-varieties of l-groups but fails to be a complete sublattice.
status_evidence.claim: The collection of quasi-varieties of ℓ-groups has cardinality 2^{aleph_0}, but no description of the idempotents of its multiplication semigroup is provided.
